lines.text: Twenty dollars. For one pair of socks.
Hikers keep buying them anyway. Here's why.
Merino fiber is so fine, it doesn't itch like normal wool.
It's naturally odor-resistant, so you can wear it again on day two.
And it stays warm, even when it's damp. Cotton doesn't.
Cheap socks cost you the hike.
Save this before your next trek, and pick your color at the link in bio.
